data.gender_notes: Lokesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who holds or rules the universe, a divine being, god. The name Lokesh carries the meaning “God of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lokesh usually hope their child will grow to embody god of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Lokesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lokesh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Lokesh" is of Sanskrit origin and is rooted in Hindu culture. The suffix "-esh" denotes "Lord" or "God" in Sanskrit, implying that Lokesh is a divine being, a god or a ruler. This name signifies power and authority, and reflects the reverence and spiritual connection the Hindus have towards their gods and divine beings.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Lokesh" symbolizes the connection between the individual and the divine consciousness that pervades the universe. It is a reminder that we are all a part of the divine creation, and that we have the potential to rule our own lives and the universe, by aligning ourselves with the divine will. It is a call to dedicate our lives to the pursuit of spiritual growth and enlightenment, and to remember that we are not alone in our journey towards self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lokesh: The one who bestows knowledge to the world (Loka- world,esh- bestows). A beacon of wisdom and enlightenment for all.

vedic_reference.note: Refers to Lord Vishnu as the ruler of the universe and the protector of the people.

historical_references.reference: Lokesh Chandra was a noted Indian historian, author, and numismatist who made significant contributions to the study of Indian coinage. He was born on 27 March 1912, in Amritsar, Punjab, British India.
Lokeshwar was a Jain Tirthankara, considered the 22nd in the present cycle of 24 Tirthankaras. He lived during the 8th century BCE in the region of Rajasthan, India.
